claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The proposed intervention is to substitute 10 at.% of Hf and Ta with Nb and V.
The modified alloy would be fabricated by arc melting and subsequent heat treatment.
The substitution will produce a solid solution.
The substitution will refine the alloy microstructure.
Replacing Hf and Ta with lighter elements will reduce the alloy's average atomic mass.
Reducing the average atomic mass will decrease the alloy density.
Solid-solution strengthening will maintain the alloy's strength after substitution.
Microstructural refinement will help maintain the alloy's strength after substitution.
The intervention will reduce density by 5%, to approximately 9.7 g cm−3.
Room-temperature strength will remain within 10% of that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Strength at 1000 °C will remain within 10% of that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed performance claim applies from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposed performance claim is limited to loading that does not exceed the yield strength of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Density reduction and strength retention may depend on the exact substitution ratio and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires strength retention within 10% of baseline, but the hypothesis is rejected only for a strength decrease greater than 15%, leaving a 10–15% decrease that violates the prediction without meeting the rejection criterion.
